chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Abi Ishaq al-Khaffaf, from al-Ya'qubi, from his father, who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام, while he was in al-Basrah, was brought a man upon whom the hadd was to be carried out. He said: when they drew near and he looked at their faces—then a group of people came forward—Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام said: “O Qanbar, see what this group is.” He said: “A man upon whom the hadd is to be carried out.” He said: when they drew near and he looked at their faces, he said: “No welcome to faces that are seen only in every evil matter. These are the superfluous among men; move them away from me, O Qanbar.”

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَا: Imam Ali عليه السلام, the Commander of the Faithful
key_terms.الْبَصْرَةِ: Basrah, the city where this event took place
key_terms.الْحَدُّ: the prescribed legal punishment being carried out
key_terms.جَمَاعَةٌ: a group or gathering of people
key_terms.فُضُولُ الرِّجَالِ: worthless or superfluous men; those of no serious moral standing in this context
key_terms.لَا مَرْحَبًا: an expression of rejection and disapproval

ai.seo_question: What did Amir al-Mu'minin عليّه السلام say about people who gathered to watch a hadd punishment?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates that Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام objected to the presence of onlookers gathering around the enforcement of a legal punishment. It highlights his disapproval of those who appear only to witness disgrace and reflects standards of dignity, public conduct, and moral seriousness in the administration of justice.
